families.summary: Small, medium, large and huge gas tanks have 46.875, 109.375, 984.375 and 3515.625 L compartments; pressure is 60 × amount ÷ volume, and a fresh tank starts at 59.4 atm at full fill.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: The compartment volume is 1.5625 × listed voxels: 4.6875, 10.9375, 98.4375 and 351.5625 units. The single Stored Gas port exchanges its network with the compartment at bias 0 and factor 1. Gas tanks run water component case 0x14 with the same ambient drift as fluid tanks, a time constant of 16.7 simulated seconds.

sections.title: Pressure and readouts
sections.body: Pressure is 60 × stored amount ÷ volume for any gas or gas mixture, so a full compartment reads 60 atm. Tank Content reads 10 × the stored amount. The tooltip's species list multiplies each gas amount by 60 and then 10, 600 per amount; inference: that is the gas's volume in litres at 1 atm. The two readouts differ by a factor of 60 for the same gas.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: A new gas tank selects the air slot; the editor offers air, oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen and a fill setting from 0 to 100. The first build adds 0.99 × fill × V of the selected gas, so a fresh tank reads 59.4 atm at full fill before any exchange, and Tank Content reads 0.99 of the litre volume. Air is split into nitrogen, oxygen and CO2 at that point. Custom tanks filled by the fluid spawner take a separate path; its tooltip says 60 atm.

findings.label: Compartment pressure law
findings.detail: All 13 fluid indices (0 to 12) enter only as liquid sum L or gas sum G, with A = L + G. Pure gas reduces to P = 60 × A ÷ V at any volume. Pure liquid in a volume up to 8 (80 L), such as a pipe network of 4, also gives 60 × A ÷ V. Pure liquid above volume 8 gives max(0.5 × A ÷ V, 7.5 × (A − V + 8)): under 0.5 atm until less than 8 (80 L) of room is left, then 7.5 atm per amount (per 75 L) up to 60 at full. Temperature does not enter. Inference from the instruction sequence; degenerate states follow the original SSE arithmetic. Report: investigation/fluids-network.md. limitations: Startup from a saved inventory or after a rebuild was not traced.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Two selectable ratios from a fixed list of eight; switching requires power.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Gearboxes use torque_component_type 1. Gear Switch off applies the Ratio Off selection, on applies Ratio On. The gearbox only changes ratio while it has electrical availability; without power it keeps the last ratio. Each change draws electricity.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: Both ratios are chosen from eight fixed options, not typed numbers: 1:-1, 1:1, 6:5, 3:2, 9:5, 2:1, 5:2 and 3:1. Internally they become the multipliers -1, 1, 0.8333333, 0.6666667, 0.5555556, 0.5, 0.4 and 0.33333334; the coupling stores the reciprocal. 1:-1 reverses direction without changing speed.

sections.title: Open measurement questions
sections.body: Which side (RPS A or RPS B) turns faster for an N:1 option, and how much torque the coupling transmits before slipping, need an in-game torque meter test.

families.summary: Charge per update is electric_magnitude × force_emitter_max_force × 0.1 × |ω| × min(|ω| ÷ 560, 0.25), with ω the shaft speed in RPS. Output shows 60 times that, the internal charge per simulated second.

sections.title: How the update works
sections.body: The generator submits its previous speed and force_emitter_max_force to its shaft group and takes the group's speed ω back, in RPS. With k = min(|ω| ÷ 560, 0.25), it deposits Q = electric_magnitude × force_emitter_max_force × 0.1 × |ω| × k into the network pool and keeps (1 − k) of its speed; that loss is the load it puts on the shaft. Charge grows with the square of speed below 140 RPS and linearly above it. Output is 60 × Q. Component updates run 60 times per simulated second, so Output is the charge deposited per simulated second while RPS holds steady. Example: a small generator at 50 RPS deposits 0.2679 per update and shows Output 16.07.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: Per RPS removed, the small, medium and large generator deposit 0.06, 2.25 and 10.625. Divided by force_emitter_max_force that is 0.06, 0.075 and 0.085. The shaft group weights each part's speed by its force_emitter_max_force, so for the same force-weighted speed removal the large generator yields 1.4167 times and the medium 1.25 times what the small one does.

sections.title: Compared with motors and the alternator
sections.body: A motor driving a generator of the same size on one shaft group returns 0.5 (small), 0.6818 (medium) or 0.8095 (large) of the motor's charge for an equal force-weighted speed change. At equal |ω| × k the modular alternator's coefficient is 0.05 against the small generator's 0.06.

sections.title: Units
sections.body: Output has no unit label. It reads internal charge per simulated second, the unit battery capacity is counted in. The generator's own buffer of 0.1 per listed voxel is a source in the pool like a battery, so it takes its share of each deposit until it is full.

limitations: Static analysis only; Q is in the internal charge unit. A conversion of internal charge to joules or watts was not recovered.
The force-weighted comparisons hold within one shaft group. How gearbox and clutch bridges, conflicting ratio loops and connector rebuilds combine groups in arbitrary networks was not decoded.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: HUD Small draws 32×32 pixels and HUD Large 96×96. HUDs use the monitor component, with the same Touch Output channels.

sections.title: Resolution by size
sections.body:
The game sets width = 32 × (voxel_max.x - voxel_min.x + 1) and height = 32 × (voxel_max.z - voxel_min.z + 1) from the definition's block bounds. The same size comes back from screen.getWidth() and screen.getHeight() in onDraw and on Touch Output number channels 1 and 2.

Sizes in pixels: HUD Small 32×32, HUD Large 96×96.

HUDs have component type 43, the monitor type, so the same resolution routine and touch setter apply. Their definitions leave the Touch Output description empty; the channel layout below is the explanation.

The listed voxel count and monitor_border do not change the pixel grid. The graphics quality setting scales the render target by 1, 2 or 4 after the size is stored, so it leaves the Lua and touch grid alone.

sections.title: Touchscreen channels
sections.body:
Touch Output is a composite. Number channels 1 and 2 carry the width and height in pixels, 3 and 4 the X and Y of the first touch, and 5 and 6 the X and Y of the second. Boolean channels 1 and 2 are on while the first and second touch are pressed. Coordinates are whole pixels from the upper left, X to the right and Y down, accepted from 0 up to the width and height inclusive.

The screen tracks at most two touches at once and ignores a third. Releasing a touch clears only its flag and leaves its last X and Y on the channels, so check the flag before using a coordinate. The touch area is the screen face inset by monitor_border on each side, stretched over the pixel grid.

sections.title: Lua callbacks
sections.body: Read the channels with input.getNumber and input.getBool in onTick, which runs once per logic tick; screen functions do nothing there. Draw in onDraw, which runs whenever a monitor draws the script and can run several times when one script drives several monitors. Composite functions do nothing in onDraw. The shipped example reads number channels 3 and 4 and boolean channel 1 in onTick and draws the matching rectangle in onDraw.

sections.title: Wiring
sections.body: Feed Video Signal from a microcontroller or camera, connect Electric and turn Power Switch on. For a touchscreen, wire Touch Output to a composite input on the microcontroller that draws the screen and its video output back to Video Signal. While the screen is switched off, every Touch Output channel reads 0.

limitations: Resolution and touch layout come from static analysis of one build and its shipped definitions; the game was not run and no touch was tested in game.

Still open: a fixed refresh rate in Hz and the delay from a touch to the next drawn frame. onDraw follows monitor rendering rather than the 60-per-second component update, and the draw scheduling, culling and caching were outside this pass.
Still open: which player or input event takes each touch slot, and how HUD hits reach the touch setter.

families.summary: Shaft-driven pumps with bias 4 × |RPS| × pump_pressure (1 small, 9 standard); at equal pressure the small pump reaches the 400 L/s bound at 5 RPS and the standard one at 0.556 RPS.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: The impeller reads the speed of the shaft on its RPS port and pushes with bias 4 × |RPS| × pump_pressure. Spinning the shaft backward pushes the same way. Unlike the electric pumps it is two-way: backpressure can push fluid back through it, and at low flow it exchanges temperature between its two networks. The shaft port records a load request of 0.1 × pump_pressure; its torque unit was not established.

sections.title: Flow
sections.body: At equal pressure the move is at most min(bias, 20) ÷ 30 amount per update, 20 L/s per unit of bias up to 400 L/s. The small pump (pump_pressure 1) reaches that ceiling at 5 RPS and the standard one (9) at 0.556 RPS. These are bounds; backpressure, fill and other ports lower the real flow.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: They pump only while the shaft turns; compare variants with the Flow Rate output in L/s.

findings.label: Equal-pressure pump flow bound
findings.value: min(max(b, 0), 20) ÷ 30 per update; small 200 L/s, large 400 L/s; 400 L/s absolute
findings.detail: With pipe networks of volume 4 on both ports at equal pressure and away from empty or full states, demand = (P_A - P_B + 2 × b) ÷ 30 and the move is at most half of it, so q ≤ min(max(b, 0), 20) ÷ 30 amount per update. The ±20 target band caps every listed pump at 2 ÷ 3 amount per update, 400 L/s. Small electric pump at full power, b = 10: 1 ÷ 3 per update, 20 amount per second, 200 L/s. Large, b = 100: 2 ÷ 3, 40 amount per second, 400 L/s. A small pump can exceed 200 L/s when upstream pressure helps it. These are bounds, not the flow a loop delivers; fill, backpressure and competing ports reduce it. Report: investigation/fluid-transport.md. families.summary: Takes half of the incoming pressure, gains 0.0000375 × pressure RPS when undamaged and charges its Electric connection; the medium turbine also joins a shaft with weight 160.

sections.title: Pressure to RPS
sections.body: After averaging, a turbine passes on half of its incoming pressure and keeps the other half's effect as speed: r0 = r + 0.0000375 × p_in. A damaged turbine gains nothing.

sections.title: Electricity
sections.body: Generator fraction k = min(r0 ÷ 10000, 0.02), reaching 0.02 at 200 RPS. Each update the Electric connection receives |r0| × 0.025 × k charge and the turbine keeps (1 - k) × r0. At 20 RPS and incoming pressure 32000 that is 0.0011236 charge per update and a submitted speed of 21.155056 RPS. Both sizes use electric_magnitude 0.025.

sections.title: Shaft
sections.body: Only the medium turbine has the RPS power connection. It submits its speed with weight 160 to the shaft's weighted average and takes back max(shaft RPS, 0). An electric motor can therefore spin it up, and props or generators can load it. 160 is a solver weight, not a torque in N m.

limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. Figures are for one part in one update. What an assembled engine settles at depends on its duct network; the Jet engines category lists that and the unit questions as open.
Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons. The shaft weight 160 is a solver weight, not a torque in N m.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Uses the same eight-option ratio list and power gate as the modular gearboxes; torque_gearbox_2 states a 4000 torque-difference limit.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Gearboxes use torque_component_type 1. Gear Switch off applies the Ratio Off selection, on applies Ratio On. The gearbox only changes ratio while it has electrical availability; without power it keeps the last ratio. Each change draws electricity.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: Both ratios are chosen from eight fixed options, not typed numbers: 1:-1, 1:1, 6:5, 3:2, 9:5, 2:1, 5:2 and 3:1. Internally they become the multipliers -1, 1, 0.8333333, 0.6666667, 0.5555556, 0.5, 0.4 and 0.33333334; the coupling stores the reciprocal. 1:-1 reverses direction without changing speed.

sections.title: Open measurement questions
sections.body: Which side (RPS A or RPS B) turns faster for an N:1 option, and how much torque the coupling transmits before slipping, need an in-game torque meter test.

sections.title: Legacy definitions
sections.body: Both legacy definitions carry torque_component_type 1 and so share the modular gearbox code path; only torque_gearbox_2's tooltip states an operating limit of 4000 torque difference.

families.summary: Mixes two liquid compartments of 20 L (2x2) or 125 L (5x5) each, moving 0.03 of the gap per update weighted by the stored liquid amount on each side.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Case 0x10 uses the liquid capacity helper for both sides: q is the stored amount of fresh water, diesel, jet fuel, oil, seawater, slurry and saturated slurry, each with weight 1, so fresh water and seawater count the same. Gas in a side counts 0. Each side passes fluid only with both its In and Out ports connected.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Per update the hotter compartment loses and the colder gains in proportion 0.03 × q_other ÷ (qA + qB), conserving qA × TA + qB × TB. Without through-flow the gap keeps 0.161 of its size after one simulated second (time constant 0.547 s). With flow, arriving liquid is mixed by the side's amount after the move, and the Out port carries the side's mixed temperature.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: Each side holds V = 0.5 × listed voxels: 2 units (20 L) for the 2x2 with 4 voxels and 12.5 units (125 L) for the 5x5 with 25. At equal fill the 5x5 has 6.25 times the q on each side. The gap still shrinks by the same 0.03 fraction per update.

sections.title: Equal-flow comparison
sections.body: At 60 L/s on each side, 0.8 fill, inlets of 100 and 20 °C and ambient 20 °C, the 2x2 emits 85.54 and 33.13 °C and the 5x5 66.02 and 46.64 °C. Temp A and Temp B read 84.68 and 33.90 °C for the 2x2, 65.68 and 46.90 °C for the 5x5. The hot side drops by 18.1 % and 42.5 % of the inlet gap; these figures include ambient loss and the game's mixing rule, so they are not a conserved-energy effectiveness. These are outputs of the report's 60 Hz model with fixed boundary networks and a prescribed flow, not game measurements or a pump rating. The interactive graph below runs the same model.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Temp A and Temp B read the stored compartment temperatures in °C after this update's exchange and ambient step. Fluid leaving the Out ports was emitted earlier in the same update, so its temperature can differ. Both compartments also drift toward the surrounding temperature by 0.001 per update, so an idle exchanger slowly settles to ambient: the leak alone has a time constant of 16.7 simulated seconds.

findings.label: Exchanger capacity q
findings.value: pure gas q = P × V ÷ 60; liquid q = stored liquid amount
findings.detail: q is the side's stored amount of its phase in native units, 10 L of liquid or 600 L of expanded gas per amount. Inference from the pressure law: pure gas has P = 60 × G ÷ V, so q = G = P × V ÷ 60 and doubling pressure doubles q at a fixed volume. At equal volume a 1 atm gas side has V ÷ 60 and a full liquid side V; at 60 atm the gas side equals the full liquid side. With gas and liquid in one side, sum the gas amounts instead of using P × V ÷ 60. Wrong-phase contents give 0 toward that side's q but still move through the ports. Report: investigation/heat-exchangers.md. families.summary: Burns diesel with manifold oxygen inside a temperature-dependent air:fuel window; best efficiency near ratio 13.6 cold and 14.0 hot, no fuel above 60 RPS.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: A cylinder produces torque only when the crank is above 2 RPS, its air:fuel ratio is inside the window 12 − 2t … 16 + 4t (t = manifold °C ÷ 100, clamped 0…1), and the crank is at or below 60 RPS. Fuel is capped by the diesel available in its fuel manifolds and intake by the oxygen in its air manifolds.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Fuel per update = RPS × 4e-6 × listed voxels × fuel throttle, which is RPS × 0.00024 × listed voxels × fuel throttle per simulated second. Intake = RPS × 2.8e-6 × listed voxels ÷ 60 × air throttle × pressure factor, where the pressure factor rises from 1 to 2 with air-manifold pressure (scale 0.01). Efficiency = speed efficiency × mixture factor; speed efficiency = clamp(4(0.02·RPS + 0.5)/(0.02·RPS + 1)² − 1, 0, 1), and the mixture factor 1 − 2(s − 0.6)² peaks at the air:fuel ratio 13.6 cold, 14.0 hot. The displayed Stoichiometric value is 2s − 1, so aim for about 0.2.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The cylinder code multiplies fuel and intake by the definition's listed voxel count: 1 for the 1x1, 27 for the 3x3 and 125 for the 5x5. At equal RPS and throttle a 3x3 cylinder therefore admits 27 times the fuel of a 1x1 and heats its manifolds correspondingly.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: With equal air and fuel throttles and no boost the ratio is 7, below the window, so the engine will not fire; reduce fuel throttle to roughly half of air throttle or add manifold pressure. Exhaust that cannot fit into the exhaust manifolds reduces torque and heat in proportion (Exhaust % in the inspection text). Above 115 °C with overheating enabled the cylinder accumulates damage every 300 updates, once per 5 simulated seconds; while damaged its torque gain halves from 80000 to 40000, and at a counter of 20 it stops producing torque.

sections.title: Open measurement questions
sections.body: Confirm the target ratio in game with the Air:Fuel Ratio inspection line; measure how manifold pressure units relate to the pressure factor; time the damage interval to check the 5-second period.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.
The fuel/air attribution of the two throttle offsets rests on the diesel and oxygen caps applied to them.
The counter at component offset 0x8 is read as damage because the overheat branch increments it (capped at 50); its other writers were not traced.

families.summary: Adds 150, 600 or 2400 to the crank inertia sum, against 0.7 for a 1x1 crank block; it smooths speed and slows starting.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Every cylinder torque impulse is divided by the summed crank inertia. The flywheels also add the same amount to a second accumulator from engine_frictionless_force, whose use was not traced.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The starter's coupling weights its own inertia (engine_max_force 0.5) against the crank inertia and only assists below 5 RPS, so a large flywheel noticeably lengthens cranking. Expect smaller RPS dips under load in exchange.

families.summary: Monitors draw 32 pixels per block of width and height, from 32×32 (Monitor 1x1) to 288×160 (Monitor 9x5). Touch Output reports that size and two touch points in pixels.

sections.title: Resolution by size
sections.body:
The game sets width = 32 × (voxel_max.x - voxel_min.x + 1) and height = 32 × (voxel_max.z - voxel_min.z + 1) from the definition's block bounds. The same size comes back from screen.getWidth() and screen.getHeight() in onDraw and on Touch Output number channels 1 and 2.

Sizes in pixels: Monitor 1x1 32×32, Monitor 1x2 64×32, Monitor 1x3 96×32, Monitor 2x2 64×64, Monitor 2x3 96×64, Monitor 3x3 96×96, Monitor 5x3 160×96, Monitor 9x5 288×160.

Follow the bounds, not the name: in Monitor 1x2, 1x3 and 2x3 the first number is the height in blocks, while 5x3 and 9x5 give the width first.

The listed voxel count and monitor_border do not change the pixel grid. The graphics quality setting scales the render target by 1, 2 or 4 after the size is stored, so it leaves the Lua and touch grid alone.

sections.title: Touchscreen channels
sections.body:
Touch Output is a composite. Number channels 1 and 2 carry the width and height in pixels, 3 and 4 the X and Y of the first touch, and 5 and 6 the X and Y of the second. Boolean channels 1 and 2 are on while the first and second touch are pressed. Coordinates are whole pixels from the upper left, X to the right and Y down, accepted from 0 up to the width and height inclusive.

The screen tracks at most two touches at once and ignores a third. Releasing a touch clears only its flag and leaves its last X and Y on the channels, so check the flag before using a coordinate. The touch area is the screen face inset by monitor_border on each side, stretched over the pixel grid.

sections.title: Lua callbacks
sections.body: Read the channels with input.getNumber and input.getBool in onTick, which runs once per logic tick; screen functions do nothing there. Draw in onDraw, which runs whenever a monitor draws the script and can run several times when one script drives several monitors. Composite functions do nothing in onDraw. The shipped example reads number channels 3 and 4 and boolean channel 1 in onTick and draws the matching rectangle in onDraw.

sections.title: Wiring
sections.body: Feed Video Signal from a microcontroller or camera, connect Electric and turn Power Switch on. For a touchscreen, wire Touch Output to a composite input on the microcontroller that draws the screen and its video output back to Video Signal. While the screen is switched off, every Touch Output channel reads 0.

families.summary: When attached, links its fluid network to the other connector's with bias 0, both directions and exchange factor 0.5; the two networks stay separate.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: With an attached connector, a network on its Fluid port and the transfer flag set, each update calls the two-port solver between the two Fluid ports: bias 0, both directions, all species and factor 0.5, which halves the per-update step limit. The connector holds no fluid and does not merge the networks, so each side keeps its own 40 L pipe pressure.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Free flow in the tooltip means no bias and no species filter. The halved step limit still applies, so it is not unlimited flow.

families.summary: Pumps heat from liquid A to liquid B by a fixed amount per update, even against the gradient, while powered and switched on.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Case 0x21 pumps only with On/Off on, electricity supplied above 0.1 of the request, and the two compartments together holding more than 0.001 capacity units. Each update it requests 0.001 electricity units, 0.06 per simulated second.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Unlike an exchanger it does not stop at equal temperatures: A loses 0.03·qB/(qA+qB) and B gains 0.03·qA/(qA+qB) every update, so B can be driven hotter than A. While q stays constant, that is 1.8·qB/(qA+qB) and 1.8·qA/(qA+qB) per simulated second. Remove heat from B with a radiator or exchanger or the transfer stalls as B climbs.

sections.title: Open measurement questions
sections.body: Electric unit cost of the 0.001 request and the capacity terms q per litre of each liquid.

families.summary: Moves at most 0.01 internal charge per update from its input network to its output network and never back. It checks no minimum charge difference.

sections.title: How the transfer works
sections.body: Each update the charger requests R = min(0.01, q_in, 1 − q_out), where q_in and q_out are the charge fractions of its two networks. It takes min(max(0, 1 − n ÷ 300) × q_in × R, E_in) from the input pool, n being its input node's EMP countdown and E_in the input pool's charge, and adds that to the output pool. Nothing moves once the output network is full or the input is empty. With infinite electricity it adds R without removing anything.

sections.title: Rates
sections.body: The cap is 0.01 per update, 0.6 per simulated second. Transfer runs even when the output is fuller than the input: at q_in = 0.5 and q_out = 0.9 it moves 0.005 per update, 0.3 per simulated second. Filling a small battery's 1600 from empty at the cap takes at least 2667 simulated seconds, so a charger suits trickle charging, not powering loads.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Use it to charge a battery from a generator bus without the battery back-feeding. Its electric node buffer is 0.01 (electric_type 6). The tooltip's significant discrepancy has no threshold in the code; the headroom and supply limits above take its place.

families.summary: Blinks for whole numbers of updates: on for trunc(60 × on time), off for trunc(60 × off time), while Control Signal is on.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: The two durations become N_on = trunc(60 × on time) and N_off = trunc(60 × off time) updates. When Control Signal changes the cycle counter restarts at 0. Otherwise the counter advances by 1 each update and wraps after N_on + N_off. The output is on while Control Signal is on and the counter is below N_on, so each cycle gives N_on updates on and N_off off. For example 0.51 s × 60 = 30.6, truncated to 30 updates.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The microprocessor Blinker is a different routine: it starts each call off and spends its wrap update off, so after the first cycle it gives one update fewer on.

families.summary: Turns on after Charge has been on for trunc(60 × charge time) updates and off after it has been off for trunc(60 × discharge time).

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: Any change of Charge clears both counters. While the output is off and Charge is on, the charge counter is compared with N_charge, the output turns on when they are equal, then the counter adds 1. While the output is on and Charge is off, the discharge counter works the same way against N_discharge. With N_charge = 60 a rising Charge at update 0 turns the output on at update 60, the 61st update including the edge. A charge time of 0 turns it on in the edge update. For example 0.51 s × 60 = 30.6, truncated to 30 updates.

families.summary: Copies its input to the output once the input has stayed unchanged for trunc(60 × delay) updates; any change restarts the count.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: With N = trunc(60 × delay), a change of Signal to Delay resets the counter to 0 and leaves the output as it was. Each following update with the input unchanged adds 1, and when the counter reaches N the output takes the input. The output therefore follows a change N updates later, and a signal that flips sooner never passes. For example 0.51 s × 60 = 30.6, truncated to 30 updates. With N = 0 the output never changes, because the counter test c < N fails at once.

families.summary: Acts only when Set or Reset changes: Set sets, Reset resets, both on toggles once. Holding both on does not keep toggling.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: On an update where Set or Reset changed: Set on and Reset off sets the output, Reset on and Set off resets it, both on toggles it, both off holds it. On an update where neither input changed the output holds, whatever the inputs are. Inputs that change together count as one change.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: To toggle repeatedly with both inputs on, pulse one of them: each new change to both on toggles once. The microprocessor JK flip-flop follows the same rule.

families.summary: Per-update PID: Control Output = Ki·S + Kp·e + Kd·(e − e_prev), with e = Setpoint − Process Variable and S the running sum of e. There is no dt, no derivative filter and no output limit.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: Each update with Active on: e = Setpoint − Process Variable, S = S + e, d = e − e_prev, and Control Output = Ki × S + Kp × e + Kd × d. Arithmetic is single precision in that order. On the first update after Active turns on, d is 0. Turning Active off sets S, e_prev and the output to 0.

sections.title: Timebase
sections.body: Nothing is multiplied by a time step. S gains 60 errors per simulated second and d is the change over one update. Converting from per-second gains (an inference about tuning conventions, not engine code): Ki = Ki_per_second ÷ 60 and Kd = 60 × Kd_per_second. With Ki = 1 and a constant error of 1, the output reaches 60 after one simulated second.

sections.title: Limits and edge cases
sections.body: max_error (pid_controller_max_error) is the only limit. When it is above 0, S is clamped to ±max_error ÷ max(1e-8, Ki), so the integral term Ki × S stays within ±max_error for positive Ki. It does not limit P, D or Control Output. A NaN or infinite output becomes 0. The derivative acts on the error, so a Setpoint step gives a one-update kick of Kd × step.

sections.title: Microprocessor PIDs
sections.body: The microprocessor PID and advanced PID run the same recurrence without the max_error clamp and without the finite-value check, so their sum and output are unbounded. Example: Kp 2, Ki 0.5, Kd 0 and a steady error of 2 give 5, 6, 7 in a microprocessor; the physical PID with max_error 1 holds S at 2 and gives 5, 5, 5.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Set max_error to bound windup when the driven part saturates. Toggle Active off to clear the stored sum. Start with small Ki: a per-update sum grows 60 times faster than a per-second integral.

findings.label: Microprocessor PID tick
findings.value: S = S + e, no clamp, no finite check

families.summary: Ignites above 0.5 RPS, then burns 0.12 × throttle × RPS L/s of jet fuel and adds 1600 × throttle × RPS pressure and 0.1 × throttle × RPS temperature per update.

sections.title: Ignition
sections.body: Combustion runs only while the chamber's RPS is strictly above 0.5. There is no pressure, temperature or spark test, so the tooltip's internal pressure threshold is in effect the compressor's job of spinning the shared RPS past 0.5.

sections.title: Fuel use
sections.body: Fuel per update is 0.0002 × RPS amount × u, with u = clamp(Throttle, 0, 1) further limited by the jet fuel in the 4 L buffer: 0.12 × u × RPS L/s, 2.4 L/s at 20 RPS and full throttle. With only 0.01 L left at 20 RPS, u drops to 0.25 and the update burns it. infinite_fuel skips the limit and the debit. Other liquids in the buffer are cleared.

sections.title: Pressure and heat
sections.body: Above 0.5 RPS: outgoing pressure = incoming + 1600 × u × RPS and outgoing temperature = incoming + 0.1 × u × RPS, in internal units; the incoming pressure is then cleared. At 20 RPS and full throttle from zero that is 32000 and 2 in one update.

sections.title: Overspeed
sections.body: With the engine_overheating setting and a second settings flag on, a chamber above 200 RPS sets a one-time flag and passes its damage + 1 to a damage routine.

limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. Figures are for one part in one update. What an assembled engine settles at depends on its duct network; the Jet engines category lists that and the unit questions as open.
Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons.
The effect of the overspeed damage on the engine was not traced.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Spins up from electricity and pushes pressure forward: q = 0.2 × (100 × RPS - pressure rise) per update, losing 0.0001 × q RPS for it.

sections.title: Starting
sections.body: With the Compressor input on and electricity connected the compressor requests 0.1 charge every update (6 per simulated second) and adds 0.01 × the supplied fraction to its RPS. Its electric_magnitude of 0 is not used. Speed is then multiplied by 0.99, enabled or not.

sections.title: Pressure and load
sections.body: After averaging with its neighbours the compressor aims for a pressure rise of 100 × RPS across itself and moves 0.2 of the shortfall from its incoming to its outgoing side. Back pressure above that target makes q negative, so pressure flows backwards and the compressor speeds up. q is a pressure transfer, not a volume flow in L/s.

sections.title: Example
sections.body: From rest with full supply the first update gives r0 = 0.0099 RPS, q = 0.198 and r_local = 0.0098802. The averaging with neighbours then changes the next state, so this is not a startup time.

limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. Figures are for one part in one update. What an assembled engine settles at depends on its duct network; the Jet engines category lists that and the unit questions as open.
Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: The basic exhaust's force times 1 + 500 × the jet fuel stored in its buffer while Afterburner is on; its branch never subtracts that fuel.

sections.title: Thrust
sections.body: Force = 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000) × a × b × (1 - Thrust Spoiler) along the exhaust's thrust axis, with altitude factor a = clamp(1 - height × 1.5 ÷ 40000, 0, 1) and afterburner multiplier b = 1 when off. At or below 1000 there is no force. No exhaust size, engine_max_force or RPS term enters; RPS matters only through the pressure the chamber adds upstream.

sections.title: Afterburner multiplier
sections.body: With the Afterburner input on and any liquid in its buffer, b = 1 + 0.5 × stored jet fuel ÷ 0.001 = 1 + 500 × stored amount. 0.001 amount (0.01 L) gives 1.5; a full 0.4 amount (4 L) buffer gives 201. The ratio has no upper clamp, so a full buffer multiplies thrust far beyond the tooltip's description, until the 100 × S cap.

sections.title: Fuel
sections.body: Jet fuel reaches the buffer through the Fuel port, which exchanges with the pipe network each update. The exhaust branch reads the stored amount but never subtracts it; only other liquids are purged. How much the port then draws from the tank depends on the network, which was not modelled.

sections.title: Force units and limit
sections.body: The force is in internal units. Before it is applied its size is limited to 100 × S, where S is a per-vehicle scale passed in by the component dispatcher, the same mechanism the control surfaces use with a limit of 5. It is applied once per update and integrated by the physics solver; do not multiply it by 60.

sections.title: Example
sections.body: At incoming pressure 16000, sea level and spoiler 0 the force is 480000; spoiler 0.5 gives 240000. With S = 1000 the cap limits both to 100000. An enabled afterburner holding 0.01 L gives 720000 before the cap.

limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. Figures are for one part in one update. What an assembled engine settles at depends on its duct network; the Jet engines category lists that and the unit questions as open.
Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons. The cap scale S is open, as the Jet engines category records.
The afterburner's steady fuel use was not recovered: the exhaust branch never subtracts jet fuel, and what its Fuel port draws depends on the external fluid network, which was not modelled.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Pushes with 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000), scaled by altitude and the Thrust Spoiler, capped at 100 × S.

sections.title: Thrust
sections.body: Force = 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000) × a × b × (1 - Thrust Spoiler) along the exhaust's thrust axis, with altitude factor a = clamp(1 - height × 1.5 ÷ 40000, 0, 1) and afterburner multiplier b = 1 when off. At or below 1000 there is no force. No exhaust size, engine_max_force or RPS term enters; RPS matters only through the pressure the chamber adds upstream.

sections.title: Altitude and spoiler
sections.body: The altitude factor falls linearly to 0 at a height of 26666.67 and is 0.625 at 10000. Reading that height as metres is an inference. Thrust Spoiler 0 keeps the whole force and 1 removes it, without changing engine speed. Above 1000 the exhaust clears its incoming pressure each update after using it.

sections.title: Force units and limit
sections.body: The force is in internal units. Before it is applied its size is limited to 100 × S, where S is a per-vehicle scale passed in by the component dispatcher, the same mechanism the control surfaces use with a limit of 5. It is applied once per update and integrated by the physics solver; do not multiply it by 60.

sections.title: Example
sections.body: At incoming pressure 16000, sea level and spoiler 0 the force is 480000; spoiler 0.5 gives 240000. With S = 1000 the cap limits both to 100000.

limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. Figures are for one part in one update. What an assembled engine settles at depends on its duct network; the Jet engines category lists that and the unit questions as open.
Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons. The cap scale S is open, as the Jet engines category records.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: The basic exhaust's force along a direction set by a powered pivot within −0.5 … 0.5 turns.

sections.title: Thrust
sections.body: Force = 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000) × a × b × (1 - Thrust Spoiler) along the exhaust's thrust axis, with altitude factor a = clamp(1 - height × 1.5 ÷ 40000, 0, 1) and afterburner multiplier b = 1 when off. At or below 1000 there is no force. No exhaust size, engine_max_force or RPS term enters; RPS matters only through the pressure the chamber adds upstream. The pivot turns the thrust axis and the lever arm; the coefficient is the same as the basic exhaust's.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Rotation Target is a standard value; supply Electric for the pivot.

sections.title: Force units and limit
sections.body: The force is in internal units. Before it is applied its size is limited to 100 × S, where S is a per-vehicle scale passed in by the component dispatcher, the same mechanism the control surfaces use with a limit of 5. It is applied once per update and integrated by the physics solver; do not multiply it by 60.

Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons. The cap scale S is open, as the Jet engines category records.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: A microcontroller in a block: each update it copies its connected inputs into an embedded logic graph, runs the graph, then copies the graph outputs back out.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: Component type 37 runs the microprocessor update. It calls every input bridge, then the graph update with the embedded graph at +0x1c0, then every output bridge. Each bridge copies one value: a Boolean input bridge reads the connected vehicle signal into a graph node, and a Boolean output bridge writes a graph output to the connected signal. Bridges with no connection do nothing.

sections.title: Ports
sections.body: The definition lists no logic nodes and no tooltip. The ports come from the bridges of the embedded graph, with number, on/off, composite, video and audio bridge types. Read the ports from the microcontroller you placed, not from the definition.

sections.title: Inside the graph
sections.body: The graph gathers every component's inputs before it runs any component, so a change moves one component per update (inference). Its components are separate routines from the physical gates: the PID has no max_error clamp, and the Blinker differs, as their part pages note.

families.summary: Charge per update rises with the square of its coupled speed up to 140, then linearly.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Case 5 adds electric_magnitude × force_emitter_max_force × 0.1 × 0.1 × |ω| × min(|ω| ÷ 560, 0.25) per update, with electric_magnitude 0.05 and force_emitter_max_force 100. The alternator then retains (1 − min(|ω| ÷ 560, 0.25)) of its speed, which is the load it puts on the belt. Multiply the charge per update by 60 for charge per simulated second.

families.summary: Belt-driven pump coupled to the crank by clutch pressure; its own speed decays by the factor 0.99 every update.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: The fluid-pump case couples the pump speed to the crank weighted by its engine_max_force (0.5) against the crank inertia, scaled by Clutch Pressure clamped between zero and one, then pumps and multiplies its speed by 0.99. Uncoupled, it keeps 0.547 of its speed after one simulated second (time constant 1.66 s).

sections.title: Flow
sections.body: The pump pushes with a bias equal to its own shaft speed in RPS and is one-way. At equal pressure it moves at most 20 L/s per RPS, reaching the 400 L/s bound at 20 RPS. Its speed is not crank RPS × clutch: it moves toward the belt speed by the clutch and inertia share each update and is then multiplied by 0.99. Without a belt group, or when damaged, it passes fluid only where pressure already pushes it. Its pump_pressure field is not read.

findings.value: min(max(b, 0), 20) ÷ 30 per update; small 200 L/s, large 400 L/s; 400 L/s absolute
findings.detail: With pipe networks of volume 4 on both ports at equal pressure and away from empty or full states, demand = (P_A - P_B + 2 × b) ÷ 30 and the move is at most half of it, so q ≤ min(max(b, 0), 20) ÷ 30 amount per update. Large, b = 100: 2 ÷ 3, 40 amount per second, 400 L/s. A small pump can exceed 200 L/s when upstream pressure helps it. These are bounds, not the flow a loop delivers; fill, backpressure and competing ports reduce it. Report: investigation/fluid-transport.md. families.summary: Pushes the crank only below 5 RPS, in proportion to the shortfall, while powered.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Case 7 runs while the starter input is on and the component is undamaged. It draws electricity through the shared helper and adds speed proportional to (5 − crank RPS), clamped at zero. Its speed is coupled to the crank with weights engine_max_force (0.5) and the crank inertia, then decays by 0.99 per update. Without coupling or drive it would keep 0.547 of its speed after one simulated second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Because assistance ends at 5 RPS and a cylinder needs more than 2 RPS plus a valid mixture, set the throttles before cranking. Large flywheels reduce how fast the starter can bring the crank up.

families.summary: Anchors only within about 1 m of terrain and ±30 degrees of upright; unanchoring resets drilling progress.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Drive the rod from a rotary table, force it down and keep drilling slurry flowing through a swivel; extract saturated slurry from the well head.

findings.label: Oil Rig Well Head · tooltip
findings.value: Once anchored to the terrain, a drill rod can be inserted into a well head to begin drilling a well. In order to drill effectively a drill rod should be driven by a rotary table and forced downward toward the terrain. A continuous supply of drilling slurry must be provided through the drill rod via a swivel, and the saturated drilling slurry extracted from the well head fluid port.
findings.detail: oil_rig_well_head: developer-authored description; intended behaviour, not a measurement.

findings.label: Oil Rig Well Head · port Anchor
findings.value: Extend / retract piles to anchor the well head to the terrain, allowing for a new well to be drilled. The well head must be close to the terrain (~1m) and upright (+-30 degrees) to be anchored. Unanchoring the well will reset any drilling progress made.
findings.detail: oil_rig_well_head: input port. Interface description.

families.summary: Deploys on signal, opens at 20 m/s, stalls below 5 m/s, and must be refolded at a workbench after use.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Hold Deploy on; it closes when the signal stops or it stalls. Size is set with the select tool.

findings.label: Vehicle Parachute · tooltip
findings.value: The parachute will deploy when receiving an on signal, and will close when not. Once deployed, it will open at a speed of 20m/s and stall when it drops below 5m/s. Once opened, the single use will be consumed and it must be returned to a workbench to be refolded. The size of the parachute can be customised by selecting this component with the select tool.
findings.detail: parachute: developer-authored description; intended behaviour, not a measurement.

findings.label: Vehicle Parachute · port Deploy
findings.value: Deploy the parachute. The parachute will close when it stalls or stops receiving an on signal.
findings.detail: parachute: input port. Interface description.

families.summary: Seventeen composite channels of position, rotation and velocity; GPS position needs electricity.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Channels 1–3 position, 4–6 Euler rotation, 7–9 linear and 10 to 12 angular velocity, 13–14 absolute speeds, 15–16 local tilts and 17 compass heading from −0.5 to 0.5. It measures along its local Y axis.

findings.label: Physics Sensor · tooltip
findings.value: Outputs physics information to a composite logic node. Requires Electric for GPS position functionality. This component is directed along its local Y axis.
findings.detail: physics_sensor: developer-authored description; intended behaviour, not a measurement.

findings.label: Physics Sensor · port Composite Output
findings.value: Outputs [1] x position, [2] y position, [3] z position, [4] euler rotation x, [5] euler rotation y, [6] euler rotation z, [7] linear velocity x, [8] linear velocity y, [9] linear velocity z, [10] angular velocity x, [11] angular velocity y, [12] angular velocity z, [13] absolute linear velocity, [14] absolute angular velocity, [15] local z tilt, [16] local x tilt and [17] compass heading (-0.5 to 0.5) to the respective composite channels.
findings.detail: physics_sensor: output port. Interface description.

families.summary: Links the fluid networks at both ends of a hose with bias 0, both directions and exchange factor 0.5; hose length adds no volume or resistance.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: A rope logic link between two anchors forms the hose. Each update a valid link calls the two-port solver between the Fluid Node networks at its two ends with bias 0, both directions, all species and factor 0.5, which halves the per-update step limit. When the far end is a hose pulley the link uses the pulley's matching port.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The anchor stores no fluid and the exchange reads no length, so a long hose moves fluid as readily as a short one.

families.summary: Takes outside air through its Fluid port. Airspeed in m/s along the part's local +X axis, the side the mouth faces, adds 0.1 × speed of bias, which acts like 2 × that much extra outside pressure; inside an enclosed compartment it is a plain port.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Case 0xf shares the fluid-update block of cases 0, 0xc and 0x17, which does nothing until the Fluid port is connected. Each update 0x140311f20 builds the state outside the port. If the scoop sits in an enclosed compartment, outside means that compartment's air, the factor is 1 and no speed term is added. Otherwise the outside is fresh air when the port is above the water surface and sea water when it is below.

sections.title: Outside pressure
sections.body:
Air pressure is (1 - 2.2413793e-05 × y)^5.3595023 with y the port's world height in metres, 1 at sea level, 0.8856 at 1000 m, 0.5289 at 5000 m and 0.2566 at 10000 m. Above 40000 m it is 0. The air is 20 units split 15.792, 4.2 and 0.007999999 across fluid indices 11, 10 and 4, the dry-air nitrogen, oxygen and carbon dioxide shares, though the code does not name them.

Under water the pressure is 30 - 29 ÷ (1 + 0.001 × depth): 1.2871 at 10 m, 3.6364 at 100 m, 15.5 at 1000 m. The outside fluid is 20 units of index 6 plus any oil the world map holds at that spot, so a submerged scoop pulls water.

sections.title: Speed term
sections.body:
The update takes the port's velocity, including spin, subtracts the wind and projects the result on the part's local X axis. The mesh mouth faces local +X, so driving mouth first in still air gives a positive speed; air entering the mouth moves along -X. Speed is in m/s: the linear speed sensor, whose output is documented in m/s, uses the same velocity calculation without conversion.

Bias = 0.1 × voxel count × that speed, clamped to -10…10; the scoop has 1 voxel, so the clamp is hit at 100 m/s. Moving tail first gives a negative bias that favors outflow from the network, and sideways motion adds nothing.

sections.title: Wind
sections.body: The subtracted vector is the vehicle's cached weather wind, so the scoop responds to airspeed rather than ground speed. Facing into a headwind raises the bias, and a tailwind as fast as the vehicle cancels it. The game samples the wind once per vehicle at its transformed origin, not at each scoop. The sample includes local weather-cell wind and is scaled by 1 - shelter, so inside a weather shelter volume it is 0. A vehicle whose parent-body link (vehicle+0x14b8) is set gets zero wind on this path.

sections.title: Flow per update and per second
sections.body:
The port routine works in pressure units where 1 is sea-level air. For a gas-filled pipe network of 8 or more volume units, away from the target-pressure and free-window clamps, the demand is (P_net - (p_out + 2 × bias)) ÷ 15 amount per update, negative meaning inflow, and inflow demand stops growing at 2 ÷ 15 × p_out. The move magnitude is at most 0.5 × factor × the absolute demand, using the network's allocation from the previous update. At exactly P_net - p_out - bias = 0 the routine instead sets demand to 0.

At sea level with the network at pressure 1, a sole scoop moves 0.0167, 0.0333, 0.05 and 0.0667 amount per update at 2.5, 5, 7.5 and 10 m/s, and stays at 0.0667 above that. The port counter stores 600 × the gas amount moved in one update (10, 20, 30 and 40), and the inspection tooltip multiplies it by 60 and shows L/s: 600, 1200, 1800 and 2400 L/s. A stationary scoop on a network an engine has pulled to 0 moves 0.0333 amount per update, 1200 L/s, so speed can double the best static intake. At altitude the maximum inflow scales with p_out while the bias does not. Unsaturated flow does not generally scale in the same way; it depends on network pressure too.

Component updates run 60 times per simulated second, so under the same assumptions the sea-level cap is 4 amount per second, shown as 2400 L/s. The still scoop into a network at 0 takes 2 amount per second (1200 L/s), and below the cap flow into a network at 1 is 0.4 × speed amount per second, 240 × speed L/s up to 10 m/s. The tooltip therefore counts 1 gas amount as 600 L. That factor is fixed and does not divide by network pressure, so the figure is not the compressed volume in the pipes. These are rates at a fixed state; a filling network raises P_net and the flow falls.

sections.title: Near volcanoes
sections.body: In air, the move is also scaled by an exchange factor. Volcanoes lower it: each active volcano adds a source with strength volcanic_heat² and radius 0.5 × eruption_radius at its position. The factor is max(0.01, 1 - volcanic_heat² × eruption_radius ÷ (2 × distance)) for the strongest source, so a hot volcano with a wide eruption radius can cut intake to 0.01 of normal near it. Away from volcanoes the factor is 1. Under water it stays 1.

sections.title: Sealed network
sections.body: The simplified demand has a zero at P_net = p_out + 2 × bias: 3 at 10 m/s, 11 at 50 and 21 at 100 or more, where the bias clamp caps it. The exact branch also gives zero demand at P_net = p_out + bias. These are mathematical zero-demand points, not a verified final pressure for a filling network.

findings.detail: The dispatcher clears its component index at 0x1405497be, makes one call through vtable slot +0x358 per iteration and increments the index at 0x1405498dd. findings.detail: After the component pass the coordinator stores 1 at scene+0x6788 (worker+0xd0) and submits the scene physics worker (update_thread_task@c_scene) at 0x1407439df. One component pass therefore corresponds to one physics tick. Report: investigation/update-rate.md. Function 0x14073f890-0x1407468e3; instruction bytes b801000000898288670000 at 0x1407439c6. findings.label: Ticks per simulated second
findings.detail: The worker converts its tick count (worker+0xd0, loaded at 0x1405e3ad7) to binary32 and divides it by this, then passes the widened result as the elapsed time to the physics world's stepSimulation slot +0x60 at 0x1405e3b16, with at most 1000 solver substeps. With tick count 1 the elapsed simulated time is 1/60 s. Report: investigation/update-rate.md. Function 0x1405e3a80-0x1405e3b4d; instruction bytes f30f5e0d6ecc5c00 at 0x1405e3aea address binary32 60 (bytes 00007042) at 0x140bb0760. Interpretation rests on retained output investigation/native/behavior/../update-rate/asm/stormworks64-physics-worker.asm:L19-L31; ../update-rate/pseudocode/0x1405e3a80.c; ../update-rate/tables.txt:L4,L13-L14. Static analysis of this executable only; no game process was run.

findings.label: Solver substep
findings.detail: The substep is 1 ÷ the worker's solver rate (worker+0xb8), or binary32 1/60 from 0x140baf98c in the fallback branch at 0x1405e3af4. The accumulator 0x140133ea0 runs whole substeps of that length. The component dispatch is outside that loop, so the solver rates 60, 120 and 180 chosen by the coordinator do not multiply component updates. Report: investigation/update-rate.md. Function 0x1405e3a80-0x1405e3b4d; instruction bytes f30f5e83b8000000 at 0x1405e3add. Interpretation rests on retained output investigation/native/behavior/../update-rate/asm/stormworks64-physics-worker.asm:L20-L31; ../update-rate/asm/stormworks64-physics-accumulator.asm. limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run and no flow was measured.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

The flow figures assume the scoop is the only port moving gas into a network of at least 8 volume units with room to spare. With several ports, the allocation gives each f·|f| ÷ Σ|f|, and the move lags the demand by one update.
Volcanoes are the producer of exchange-factor sources found in this build. The search identified that writer but did not exhaustively exclude every other writer to the list.
The L/s figure on the inspection tooltip is a fixed display factor of 600 L per gas amount. It does not measure the compressed gas volume in the network.

families.summary: A legacy classic engine: the same update as the diesel engines with shaft weight 50, but no fuel, air, coolant or exhaust port and a starter factor of 0.

sections.title: How the update works
sections.body: turbine.xml has component type 5, so the game builds it with the same constructor and update as the diesel engines, not the jet update. engine_max_force 100000 gives shaft weight W = 50 at Max Power 100 %. Throttle is clamped to 0 to 1, although the tooltip describes -1 to 1, and the RPS Limiter, 0.99 retention, heating and overheat rules match the diesels.

sections.title: Why it does not run on its own
sections.body: The definition has four ports: RPS, Starter, Throttle and Electric. Nothing connects to the internal diesel or intake compartments, which start empty, so the supply gate holds the effective throttle at 0. electric_magnitude 0 makes the starter request 0, even with infinite electricity. Derived from the traced paths, not tested in game: a new turbine at rest does not start itself. With infinite_fuel on and its shaft spun above 2 RPS by another component, it gains speed like a diesel with W = 50.

sections.title: Shaft and load
sections.body: It still exchanges speed with its shaft group at weight 50, so on a shared shaft it adds 0.99 retention like any classic engine and heats at 0.0075 × |r| °C per update.

findings.label: Turbine Engine · engine_max_force
findings.detail: turbine: definition attribute engine_max_force. Read by the same classic engine update as the diesels: shaft weight 100000 × Max Power ÷ 2000 = 50 at full Max Power. An internal solver weight, not a torque in N m.

findings.label: Turbine Engine · electric_magnitude
findings.detail: turbine: definition attribute electric_magnitude. Starter charge factor; 0 makes the classic starter request 0.

findings.label: Legacy turbine shaft weight

findings.label: Component updates per simulated second
findings.detail: One component update per component, then one physics tick that advances simulated time by 1/60 s. For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

sections.title: Fluid through the hose
sections.body: The Hose links the fluid network at its base (Fluid) to the one at its end piece through the two-port solver: bias 0, both directions, factor 1, all species. It adds no compartment of its own, and the exchange does not read the current length, so a longer hose neither stores more fluid nor restricts flow more.

families.summary: Hold either interact action to pump: bias 3, one-way, with a smoothed handle factor; at most 60 L/s at equal pressure.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Holding an interact action sets the handle target to 1, and a smoothing controller with duration 60 moves the factor h toward it. While h is above 0.01 the pump calls the two-port solver with bias pump_pressure = 3 and factor h, one-way, all species. Released, h falls back, and at or below 0.01 nothing moves. The pump holds no fluid; its ports connect straight to the pipe networks.

sections.title: Flow
sections.body: At equal pressure between two pipe networks the bound is min(3, 20) ÷ 30 = 0.1 amount per update, 60 L/s at h = 1, against 200 L/s for the small electric pump. Backpressure, fill and other ports lower it, and backpressure cannot reverse it.

findings.label: Equal-pressure pump flow bound
findings.value: min(max(b, 0), 20) ÷ 30 per update; small 200 L/s, large 400 L/s; 400 L/s absolute
findings.detail: With pipe networks of volume 4 on both ports at equal pressure and away from empty or full states, demand = (P_A - P_B + 2 × b) ÷ 30 and the move is at most half of it, so q ≤ min(max(b, 0), 20) ÷ 30 amount per update. The ±20 target band caps every listed pump at 2 ÷ 3 amount per update, 400 L/s. Small electric pump at full power, b = 10: 1 ÷ 3 per update, 20 amount per second, 200 L/s. Large, b = 100: 2 ÷ 3, 40 amount per second, 400 L/s. A small pump can exceed 200 L/s when upstream pressure helps it. sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: On the first build the spawner adds min(free room, 0.99 × fill × V) of the selected fluid to the compartment it sits in, where V is that compartment's volume. findings.label: Compartment pressure law
findings.detail: All 13 fluid indices (0 to 12) enter only as liquid sum L or gas sum G, with A = L + G. Pure gas reduces to P = 60 × A ÷ V at any volume. Pure liquid in a volume up to 8 (80 L), such as a pipe network of 4, also gives 60 × A ÷ V. Pure liquid above volume 8 gives max(0.5 × A ÷ V, 7.5 × (A − V + 8)): under 0.5 atm until less than 8 (80 L) of room is left, then 7.5 atm per amount (per 75 L) up to 60 at full. Temperature does not enter. Inference from the instruction sequence; degenerate states follow the original SSE arithmetic. Report: investigation/fluids-network.md. families.summary: Cools its fluid toward the surrounding temperature at 0.003 per update, more when exposed to airflow.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: The passive radiator shares case 9 with the electric radiators and the fluid heat sink. Without a fan, its only boost is airflow: outside an enclosed compartment the multiplier becomes 1 + min(2, air speed ÷ 40).

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Connect both fluid ports; with either port unconnected the cooling step is skipped. Place it on the exterior of a moving vehicle to use the airflow term.

sections.title: Per-second rate
sections.body: At 60 updates per simulated second the passive term leaves 0.835 of the gap to ambient after one second (time constant 5.55 s). At the airflow cap the multiplier is 3, which leaves 0.581 (1.84 s).

sections.title: Volume
sections.body: The compartment volume equals the listed voxels, 9 units of 10 L.

sections.title: Flow through the radiator
sections.body:
Each update the radiator exchanges with its Fluid A network, then its Fluid B network, then cools. Arriving water is mixed by the radiator's amount after the move, and below 0.01 amount per update a direct exchange also moves temperature through the ports. Its volume is capacity: in a pumped loop it need not stay full, and its water settles cooler than the coolant manifold.

For one radiator fed at a fixed inlet temperature with flow q and stored water A, the outlet sits q ÷ (k × A + (1 + k) × q) of the way from ambient to the inlet, with k = 0.003 × (1 + fan). With 9 units of water, 200 L/s and a full fan that is 83.90 °C out for 100 °C in at 20 °C ambient, a 16.10 °C drop. The cooling capacity calculator's finite-flow mode steps whole loops.

findings.detail: Case 9 (fluid_radiator, fluid_radiator_electric, fluid_radiator_electric_5, fluid_heat_sink) moves the radiator compartment toward the surrounding temperature by this value × (1 + fan), only while both fluid ports are connected. Function 0x1403ef860-0x1403f51f4; it reads binary32 0.003 (bytes a69b443b) at 0x140baf918. Interpretation rests on retained output investigation/native/behavior/asm/water.asm:L3657-L3661 (case 9). findings.label: Recipient amount in temperature mixing
findings.detail: After a port move the recipient's total (+0x40) is read after it has grown by the packet q, then q is added again for the divisor: T = (A' × T + q × T_donor) ÷ (A' + q), with A' the amount after the move. The two-port solver does the same at 0x1402ee017 and 0x1402ee4b8. This weighting differs from ordinary mixing: 1 unit at 20 °C receiving 0.5 at 100 °C ends at 40 °C, not 46.7 °C. findings.label: Radiator outlet at fixed flow
findings.value: T_out - T_amb = q ÷ (k × A + (1 + k) × q) × (T_in - T_amb)
findings.detail: One radiator receiving q per update from an inlet at fixed temperature, discharging q, then cooling with k = 0.003 × (1 + fan), with water amount A after discharge and q ≥ 0.01: mixing weight q ÷ (A + 2q) = 0.034483 for the example below. Stored radiator temperature after the cooling step = (1 - k) × the same fraction. Example: A = 9, q = 1 ÷ 3 (200 L/s), fan 2, k = 0.009, inlet 100 °C, ambient 20 °C: outlet 83.90 °C, stored 83.32 °C, a drop of 16.10 °C across the radiator. Report: investigation/fluid-transport.md. findings.label: Ticks per simulated second
findings.detail: The worker converts its tick count (worker+0xd0, loaded at 0x1405e3ad7) to binary32 and divides it by this, then passes the widened result as the elapsed time to the physics world's stepSimulation slot +0x60 at 0x1405e3b16, with at most 1000 solver substeps. findings.detail: The substep is 1 ÷ the worker's solver rate (worker+0xb8), or binary32 1/60 from 0x140baf98c in the fallback branch at 0x1405e3af4. sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Open and enclosed pipes are both type 6. The network builder follows matching fluid faces through either kind and gives the whole connected run one compartment of volume 4, 40 L, no matter how many blocks it spans. families.summary: rudder_surface_area 8, 20, 40, 70 and 120 across the five wing sizes. The air force scales linearly with it, and the wing term lifts even at zero angle of attack.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: At the same body mass, airspeed, altitude and angle, the computed wing force scales linearly with rudder_surface_area: 8, 20, 40, 70 and 120, or 1, 2.5, 5, 8.75 and 15 times the small wing. The application cap can limit the gain on a light craft. The listed voxel count is not a multiplier.

sections.title: Wing lift
sections.body: Wing sections have rudder_type 1. On top of the normal airspeed they get a wing term 3 × c^5 × g, where c is the cosine between the direction of travel and the wing's forward axis (the reverse of dynamic_rotation_axes) and g rises from 0 at 15 m/s to 1 at 40 m/s. That term gives lift with the wing level in the airflow. Travelling backwards along that axis removes it. Wings have no Rotation input, so their angle to the airflow comes from how they are mounted and how the craft flies.

sections.title: Example
sections.body: A small wing section (area 8) on a body of mass 1000 at sea level, 30 m/s and 10° angle of attack gets a normal force of 594.2 internal units: 585.1 lift and 103.2 drag. The XXL wing makes 15 times that under the same conditions.

findings.label: Solver force integration
findings.detail: Solver-body setup multiplies the total force by inverse mass and then by the solver substep at 0x14012874b. The force stays in the accumulator for every substep of the outer step and is cleared afterwards (0x140133bb0). Report: investigation/control-surfaces.md. findings.label: Surface force unit
findings.detail: The routine produces a force that Bullet accumulates and integrates with inverse mass × substep. The refresh is once per component update (60 per simulated second), so the force is not multiplied by 60. Mass is not calibrated to kilograms, so the force is not labelled in newtons. Report: investigation/control-surfaces.md. findings.label: lift_force in the surface force
findings.detail: The complete rudder update has no load from tuning object +0x90 and no call to its accessor; the area coefficient is the fixed 24. lift_force 0.25 is therefore not a multiplier of this force. Other users of the field elsewhere in the executable are outside this check. Report: investigation/control-surfaces.md. Inputs: native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1403dfd20@0x1403e1120, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x140293a40@0x140b53ad0.
